sections.title: Amazon RDS Overview: Managed Databases, Storage Auto Scaling & RDS Custom
sections.objective: Explain why RDS is preferred over self-managed databases on EC2, and choose between RDS features such as storage auto scaling, Multi-AZ, read replicas and RDS Custom for a given scenario.

sections.title: Amazon RDS Read Replicas & Multi-AZ (scalability, DR, network cost)
sections.objective: Distinguish read replicas from Multi-AZ deployments, including replication type, failover behavior, scaling use cases and cross-AZ versus cross-region network costs.

sections.title: Amazon Aurora: Architecture, HA, Endpoints & Serverless
sections.objective: Explain Aurora's shared-storage HA design, endpoints and scaling options, and select Aurora Serverless or custom endpoints when workload patterns require them.

sections.title: Aurora Global Database, Machine Learning & Babelfish
sections.objective: Choose between cross-region read replicas and Aurora Global Database for DR, and identify when Aurora ML or Babelfish applies.

sections.title: RDS & Aurora Backups, Restore Options, Cloning & Security
keyTopics: Stopped DB still billed for storage
sections.objective: Choose backup, restore and cloning options that meet retention and RPO needs, and apply RDS/Aurora encryption and authentication controls correctly.

sections.title: Amazon RDS Proxy
sections.objective: Determine when to insert RDS Proxy in an architecture to pool connections, cut failover time and enforce IAM-based access, and recognize its VPC-only constraint.

sections.title: Amazon ElastiCache: Overview, Caching Patterns & Security
sections.objective: Select ElastiCache to offload read-heavy databases or store sessions, choose Redis versus Memcached from durability and HA requirements, and pick the right caching strategy.

sections.title: ElastiCache Redis Use Case: Gaming Leaderboards
sections.objective: Recognize Redis sorted sets as the exam answer for real-time leaderboards requiring uniqueness and ordering.

notes:
Exam emphasis (per SAA-C03 guide): Task 3.3 (high-performing databases — read replicas, caching, engines, capacity), Task 2.2 (HA/DR — Multi-AZ, failover, RDS Proxy, DR strategy/RTO), Task 4.3 (cost — Aurora vs RDS pricing, stopped DB storage cost, serverless, snapshot vs restore).

High-yield contrasts to drill: read replicas (ASYNC, scaling reads, SELECT only) vs Multi-AZ (SYNC, single DNS, failover only, not scaling); same-region replica replication is free but cross-region costs; restore always creates a new DB; unencrypted master -> replicas cannot be encrypted (snapshot-restore to encrypt); no SSH except RDS Custom.

Plausible distractors: assuming Multi-AZ boosts read performance; assuming read replicas give automatic failover; expecting ElastiCache to encrypt without Redis AUTH/SSL; assuming RDS Proxy is publicly reachable.

Tutor background (not in source): Aurora Global Database write-forwarding and Backtrack are Aurora-only; Aurora Serverless v2 for variable workloads. Pages 165-169 overlap section 1 boundary intentionally by topic grouping.
